{{short description|none}}
This is a list of well-known [[dimensionless quantities]] illustrating their variety of forms and applications. The tables also include [[number|pure numbers]], dimensionless ratios, or [[dimensionless physical constant]]s; these topics are discussed in the article.

==Biology and medicine==
{| class="wikitable sortable"
|-
! scope="col" | Name
! scope="col" | Standard symbol
! scope="col" class="unsortable" | Definition
! scope="col" | Field of application
|-
| [[Basic reproduction number]]       || <math>R_0</math>     || number of infections caused on average by an infectious individual over entire infectious period  || [[epidemiology]] 
|-
| [[Body fat percentage]] || || total mass of fat divided by total body mass, multiplied by 100 || biology
|-
| [[Kt/V]]                 || ''Kt''/''V''      ||  || [[medicine]] ([[hemodialysis]] and [[peritoneal dialysis]] treatment; dimensionless [[time]])
|-
| [[Waist–hip ratio]] || || waist circumference divided by hip circumference || biology
|-
| [[Physical attractiveness#Waist-to-chest ratio|Waist-to-chest ratio]] || || waist circumference divided by chest circumference  || biology
|-
| [[Waist-to-height ratio]] || || waist circumference divided by height || biology
|}

| [[Activity coefficient]]         || <math>\gamma</math>  || <math> \gamma= \frac {{a}}{{x}} </math>
| || [[chemistry]] (Proportion of "active" molecules or atoms)
|-
| [[Arrhenius equation|Arrhenius number]]    || <math>\alpha</math>  || <math>\alpha = \frac{E_a}{RT} </math> 
|[[Svante Arrhenius]]|| [[chemistry]] (ratio of [[activation energy]] to [[thermal energy]])<ref name="berkley">{{cite web |title=Table of Dimensionless Numbers |url=http://www.cchem.berkeley.edu/gsac/grad_info/prelims/binders/dimensionless_numbers.pdf |access-date=2009-11-05}}</ref>

| [[Atomic weight]]       || ''M''      || 
| || [[chemistry]] ([[mass]] of one [[atom]] divided by the [[atomic mass constant]], {{val|1|ul=Da}})
|-
| [[Bodenstein number]]   || Bo or Bd || <math>\mathrm{Bo} = vL/\mathcal{D} = \mathrm{Re}\, \mathrm{Sc} </math>  
|[[Max Bodenstein]]|| [[chemistry]] ([[Residence time distribution|residence-time]] distribution; similar to the axial [[mass transfer]] [[Peclet number]])<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Becker | first1 = A. | last2 = Hüttinger | first2 = K. J. | doi = 10.1016/S0008-6223(97)00175-9 | title = Chemistry and kinetics of chemical vapor deposition of pyrocarbon—II pyrocarbon deposition from ethylene, acetylene and 1,3-butadiene in the low temperature regime | journal = Carbon | volume = 36 | issue = 3 | page = 177 | year = 1998 }}</ref>
|-
| [[Damköhler numbers]]|| Da     ||<math> \mathrm{Da} = k \tau</math>
|[[Gerhard Damköhler]]|| [[chemistry]] (reaction time scales vs. residence time)
|-
| [[Hatta number]]         || Ha    || <math>\mathrm{Ha} = \frac{N_{\mathrm{A}0}}{N_{\mathrm{A}0}^{\mathrm{phys}}} </math> 
|Shirôji Hatta (1895–1973)|| [[chemical engineering]] ([[adsorption]] enhancement due to [[chemical reaction]])
|-
| [[Jakob number]]         || Ja      ||<math>\mathrm{Ja} = \frac{c_p (T_\mathrm{s} - T_\mathrm{sat}) }{\Delta H_{\mathrm{f}} }</math>
| || [[chemistry]] (ratio of [[Sensible heat|sensible]] to [[Enthalpy of vaporization|latent energy]] absorbed during liquid-vapor [[phase transition|phase change]])<ref>{{cite book |last=Incropera |first=Frank P. |title= Fundamentals of heat and mass transfer |url=https://archive.org/details/fundamentalsheat00incr_869 |url-access=limited |page=[https://archive.org/details/fundamentalsheat00incr_869/page/n383 376] |year=2007 |publisher=John Wiley & Sons, Inc|isbn=978-0-470-05554-0 }}</ref>
|-
| [[pH]]                   || <math>\mathrm{pH}</math> || <math>\mathrm{pH} = - \log_{10}(a_{\textrm{H}^+})</math> 
| || [[chemistry]] (the measure of the [[acid]]ity or [[Base (chemistry)|basicity]] of an [[aqueous solution]])
|-
| [[van 't Hoff factor]]   || ''i''     ||<math> i = 1 + \alpha (n - 1)</math>
|[[Jacobus Henricus van 't Hoff]]|| [[quantitative analysis (chemistry)|quantitative analysis]] ([[Freezing-point depression|''K''<sub>f</sub>]] and [[Boiling point elevation|''K''<sub>b</sub>]])
|-
| [[Wagner number]]       || Wa     ||<math>\mathrm{Wa} = \frac{\kappa}{l} \frac{\mathrm{d}\eta}{\mathrm{d}i}</math>
| || [[electrochemistry]] (ratio of [[electrochemical kinetics|kinetic]] polarization resistance to solution ohmic resistance in an [[electrochemical cell]])<ref>{{cite book |last1=Popov |first1=Konstantin I. |last2=Djokić |first2=Stojan S. |last3=Grgur |first3=Branimir N. |title=Fundamental Aspects of Electrometallurgy |date=2002 |publisher=[[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]] |location=Boston, MA |isbn=978-0-306-47564-1 |pages=101–102}}</ref>
|-
| [[Weaver flame speed number]] || Wea    ||<math>\mathrm{Wea} = \frac{w}{w_\mathrm{H}} 100</math>  
| || [[combustion]] ([[laminar flow|laminar]] burning [[velocity]] relative to [[hydrogen]] gas)<ref>{{cite book| last1 = Kuneš | first1 = J.| chapter = Technology and Mechanical Engineering| doi = 10.1016/B978-0-12-416013-2.00008-7| title = Dimensionless Physical Quantities in Science and Engineering| pages = 353–390| year = 2012| isbn = 978-0-12-416013-2}}</ref>
|}

=== Other ===
{| class="wikitable sortable"
|-
! scope="col" | Name
! scope="col" | Standard symbol
! scope="col" class="unsortable" | Definition
!Named after
! scope="col" | Field of application
|-
| [[Fine-structure constant]] || <math>\alpha</math> ||<math>\alpha = \frac{e^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 \hbar c}</math>
| || [[quantum electrodynamics]] (QED) ([[coupling constant]] characterizing the strength of the [[electromagnetic interaction]])
|-
| [[Havnes parameter]]         ||  <math> P_H </math>    || <math> P_H = \frac{Z_d n_d}{n_i} </math> 
|O. Havnes|| In [[dusty plasma]] physics, ratio of the total charge <math> Z_d </math> carried by the dust particles  <math> d </math> to the charge carried by the ions  <math> i </math>, with  <math> n </math> the number density of particles
|-
| [[Helmholtz number]]         ||  <math> He </math>    || <math> He = \frac{\omega a}{c_0} = k_0a </math> 
|[[Hermann von Helmholtz]]|| The most important parameter in duct [[acoustics]]. If <math>\omega</math> is the dimensional [[frequency]], then <math> k_0 </math> is the corresponding free field [[wavenumber]] and <math> He </math> is the corresponding dimensionless frequency <ref>S.W. RIENSTRA, 2015, Fundamentals of Duct Acoustics, Von Karman Institute Lecture Notes</ref>
|-
| [[Lundquist number]] || ''S''    || <math>S = \frac{\mu_0LV_A}{\eta}</math> 
|Stig Lundqvist || [[plasma physics]] (ratio of a resistive time to an [[Alfvén wave]] crossing time in a plasma)
|-
| [[Perveance]]          ||   ''K''    || <math>{K} = \frac{{I}}{{I_0}}\,\frac{{2}}{{\beta}^3{\gamma}^3} (1-\gamma^2f_e)</math> 
| || [[Charged particle|charged particle transport]] (measure of the strength of space charge in a charged particle beam)
|-
| [[Pierce parameter]]     || <math>C</math>        || <math>C^3=\frac{Z_c I_K}{4 V_K}</math> 
| || [[Traveling wave tube]]
|-
| [[Beta (plasma physics)|Beta]] ||  <math>\beta</math> || <math>\beta = \frac{n k_B T}{B^2/2\mu_0} </math> 
| || [[Plasma (physics)|Plasma]] and [[fusion power]]. Ratio of plasma thermal pressure to magnetic pressure, controlling the level of turbulence in a magnetised plasma.
|-
| [[Poisson's ratio]]      || <math>\nu</math>  || <math>\nu = -\frac{\mathrm{d}\varepsilon_\mathrm{trans}}{\mathrm{d}\varepsilon_\mathrm{axial}} </math> 
| || [[elasticity (physics)|elasticity]] (strain in transverse and longitudinal direction)
|-
| [[Q factor]] ||  ''Q''    || <math>Q = 2 \pi f_r \frac{\text{Energy Stored}}{\text{Power Loss}}</math>  
| || [[physics]], [[engineering]] ([[Damping ratio]] of [[oscillation|oscillator]] or [[resonator]]; [[energy]] stored versus energy lost)
|-
| [[Relative density]]     || ''RD''    || <math>RD = \frac{\rho_\mathrm{substance}}{\rho_\mathrm{reference}}</math> 
| || [[hydrometer]]s, material comparisons (ratio of [[density]] of a material to a reference material—usually [[water]])
|-
| [[Permeability (electromagnetism)|Relative permeability]] || <math>\mu_r</math> || <math>\mu_r = \frac{\mu}{\mu_0}</math> 
| ||  [[magnetostatics]] (ratio of the permeability of a specific medium to free space)
|-
| [[Relative permittivity]] || <math>\varepsilon_r</math> || <math>\varepsilon_{r} = \frac{C_{x}} {C_{0}}</math> 
| || [[electrostatics]] (ratio of [[capacitance]] of test [[capacitor]] with [[dielectric]] material versus [[vacuum]])
|-
| [[Specific gravity]] || ''SG''    ||
| || (same as [[Relative density]])
|-
| [[Stefan number]]        || Ste    ||<math>\mathrm{Ste} = \frac{c_p \Delta T}{L}</math>
|[[Josef Stefan]]|| [[phase transition|phase change]], [[thermodynamics]] (ratio of [[sensible heat]] to [[latent heat]])
|-
| [[Strain (materials science)|Strain]]      || <math>\epsilon</math> ||<math>\epsilon = \cfrac{\partial{F}}{\partial{X}} - 1</math>
| || [[materials science]], [[elasticity (physics)|elasticity]] (displacement between particles in the body relative to a reference length)
|-
| [[Erlang (unit)|Erlang]]      || <math>E</math> || <math> E = \lambda h </math>
| [[Agner Krarup Erlang]] || [[telephony]] (a measure of [[offered load]] on a [[telephone line|telephone circuit]])
|}
